identity_check.front_facing_teal_robot: yes - symmetric teal body panel viewed head-on
identity_check.two_antennae: present but loosely read - two 4px-wide navy prongs continuous with the outline at the top corners; could equally read as ears or a frame notch
identity_check.no_ground_shadow: yes - nothing below the bottom outline

parent_review.observations: I opened the delivered PNG at 1x and the 8x-on-white inspection view myself. It is a very simple blocky robot with only three colors. The sprite meets every brief requirement both by measurement and visually. Its SHA-256 equals reference.png, so the reference match is trivial. The specialist's review file is a retained inspection record. It covers all 10 views and has pass verdicts for q_mech and q_visual, and its own observations agree with mine.

limitations: PixelLab transport was mocked. The output is byte-identical to reference.png by design, so it does not show that any new artwork was generated.
The antennae are minimal blocky prongs fused to the outline, so whether they count as antennae is a judgment call.
The specialist reports that the navy outline loses contrast on dark navy backgrounds such as #202838.
The specialist recorded projection 'side' and nearest-neighbour upscaling as its own proposals, not user decisions.
No engine import was done because the brief did not require one.
The specialist left draft files in .pixl-work/ (plan-r1.px, nominate-r10.px).
The parent did not independently re-run the full PIXL workflow or state validation. The parent's checks were limited to opening the files and running asset_check on the output and on reference.png.
